minutes.headline: Parks Commission scored three Marshall Park design firms and will interview all three on Aug 21; beach house sign decision deferred.
minutes.summary: The commission approved a resident's request to plant a tree at McNelly field, with the facilities director approving the final location. It reviewed sign quotes for the Beach House and took no action, asking for more design options for October. It tallied individual scores for three Marshall Park design proposals and agreed to interview all three at the next meeting, which will start at 6:30.

attendees.role: chair (presiding; ran the agenda and the sign presentation)

public_comment.topic: Suggested the Parks Commission be among the first to use the contracted grant-writing services line in the general government budget, by taking grant proposals to the town manager.

votes.motion: Allow Dan Lincoln to plant a tree at McNelly field, with the final location approved by Chris Ruth.
votes.outcome: passed (roll call: Karen, Chris, Tim and Anita each voted aye; no opposition heard)
passed (roll call: Karen, Chris, Tim and Anita aye)

budget_items.topic: Beach House sign: Turning Leaf Designs flat sign
budget_items.what_was_said: A flat sign from the Lunenburg contractor was quoted at an approximate price; the town would likely install it itself.

budget_items.topic: Beach House sign: Add a Sign quote
budget_items.what_was_said: The quote covered the sign, a design fee, and removal of the old sign plus installation. Members thought the installation price was high given only a few screws hold the old sign.
A carved sign of the same size was quoted at a much higher price. Members said they did not need a carved sign.

budget_items.topic: Dillis and Roy donation for the Beach House sign
budget_items.what_was_said: A local business offered to cover the cost of the sign. The commission wants to accept the offer, possibly as a single gift once the design is settled.
Dillis and Roy would likely pay the vendors directly, since both are already town vendors and only need an updated insurance certificate.
A member said the grants the commission has pursued could potentially bring in a large sum.

A resident said a line item in the general government budget funds contracted grant help, under the town manager's purview. He said departments would bring grant proposals to the town manager, who decides how much to commit from it.

decisions.decision: No vote or action on the Beach House sign. The chair will ask Turning Leaf for a larger flat-sign price and design and work with Add a Sign on a softer design. The item returns at the October meeting.
Karen will tell Dillis and Roy the commission plans to accept their offer, and will update the beach staff and the family of the person the building honors.
All three Marshall Park firms will be interviewed on Aug 21.
The Aug 21 meeting will start at 6:30 rather than 7:00 to leave time for reference-check discussion.
Members will send interview questions to the chair by Tuesday morning so the same questions go to all three firms. Firms will be asked for seven hard copies plus a digital copy of any handouts.
The commission will contact the town manager to learn what process is required to use the grant-assistance funds.
The railings will be sanded and repainted. The chair will clean the building exterior before the painters arrive.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission agreed to interview all three Marshall Park design firms on Aug 21, after tallying individual scores for the proposals.
The Aug 21 meeting will start at 6:30 instead of 7:00 to leave time for reference-check discussion.
The commission took no action on the Beach House sign and asked for more design options; the item returns in October.
A roll call vote allowed a resident to plant a tree at McNelly field, with the facilities director approving the final location.
After public comment, the commission will ask the town manager what process is needed to use the grant-assistance funds.

why_it_matters: Marshall Park is a town park, and the choice of a design firm shapes what is later proposed, funded and brought to residents for a vote.
The Beach House sign is on track to be paid for by a local business donation, which would keep its cost off the town's budget, though the design and payment route are not settled.
watch_next: Aug 21 meeting at 6:30: interviews of all three Marshall Park design firms.
October meeting: the Beach House sign returns with more design options.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the one non-procedural vote (the tree planting, 4-0), the Marshall Park interviews, the 6:30 start on Aug 21 and the acceptance of the Dillis & Roy offer. They differ on who chaired (ours says Karen, the official minutes say Anita Scheipers), and the official minutes omit the sign prices, the railings, the interview logistics and the grant-assistance follow-up.
